newsitem.title: USA: Ice on Illinois, Mississippi Rivers slows barges.
newsitem.headline: Ice on Illinois, Mississippi Rivers slows barges.

text.p: Floating ice on the Illinois and Mississippi Rivers was significantly slowing barge traffic Wednesday, grain merchandisers and river officials said.

"We do have a problems with ice,"said Ron Fournier, chief public affairs officer for the Army Corps of Engineers in Rock Island, Ill. "We do have delays getting in and out of the locks, and this will continue as long as temperatures stay well below freezing," he said.
Problems with icing were particularly acute on the stretch of the Mississippi River between St. Louis, Mo. and Cairo, Ill. and a lock near Peoria, Ill., river dealers said.
The ice thickness around Peoria Lake was said to be up to 12 inches thick in some spots, which has prevented barges from moving past that area, cash sources said.
"There are still some tows that are getting through, but, it is very slow right now," said a Hennepin, Ill. grain dealer, located on the Illinois River.
The ice caused several harbor services to shut down, which has slowed the positioning of barges at grain elevators.
Floating ice was causing delays on the Mississippi between Cairo and St. Louis, and several towboats were reported aground or sitting on ice, river sources said.
Several consecutive days of warmer temperatures will be needed to alleviate ice blockages on both rivers, Fournier and grain dealers said.

However, forecasters show that after a brief warming period on Wednesday, frigid air will return to much of the Midwest on Thursday. Low temperatures were seen dipping to minus 10 degrees Farhenheit in the next several days, forecasters said.
Another sustained blast of subzero temperatures most likely means that problems with floating ice will continue and barge traffic could come to a halt on the Illinois, dealers said.
